newsitem.title: USA: CME to add two butter futures contract months.
newsitem.headline: CME to add two butter futures contract months.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said it would add two contract months to its butter futures and options effective Monday, January 6.

The Agricultural Oversight Committee approved adding September and November contracts, making a total of six contract months. A CME official said the move was prompted by industry interest in trading more distant months.
The CME re-introduced butter futures trading in September 1996 after a 20-year absence, with trading in February, April, June and July contracts.
The CME also said the following revisions would apply to deliveries of butter against futures contracts beginning in September 1997:
1. Payment for futures deliveries must be made to the Clearing House on the first business day after the buyer receives a delivery notice instead of the second day.
2. USDA grading certificates used in deliveries must be no more than six months old, compared with no restriction previously.
3. Butter delivered against futures contracts must be no more than 10 months old, versus no age requirement previously.
